ds: By following the directions of simple ideas and discoveries, one can be swept into all sorts of adventures.

t: Scholarship and Faith: Insights from My BYU Experience
ds: BYU implements a unique form of teaching centered around scholarship and faith that draws us closer to the Savior’s example.
Access to a higher education of spiritual knowledge allows us to transcend our struggles and flaws and become more like our Savior.
By “Pointing Our Souls to Christ,” we gain divine help and develop a closeness to Him that strengthens us on our journey to our Heavenly home.

t: A Life Centered on Jesus Christ
ds: True joy comes when we focus on what is within our control and then center and recenter our faith and life on Jesus Christ.

When you love your neighbor as yourself, despite your own biases and prejudices, we can build the kingdom of God on the earth.
We can become peacemakers to those around us by emulating the Savior and becoming representatives of the Prince of Peace.
We can do our part to create a beloved and hopeful community through everyday acts and acceptance of others.

t: Dare to Be Different: Preserving the Distinctive Light of Religious Universities
ds: While many universities are known for their academic achievements, BYU must strive to be different with both an academic and spiritual focus.

Justin Collings shares six things we should seek in order to come unto the Savior and fulfill BYU’s divine destiny as a school in Zion.

t: The Science of the Beloved Community
ds: Forum address delivered by American journalist and science correspondent, Shankar Vedantam, centered on how to build a beloved community.

t: “A Saint Through the Atonement of Christ the Lord”
ds: Elder Jeffrey R. Holland explains how, throughout life’s adversity, we can still become “a saint through the atonement of Christ the Lord.”

t: Thoughts of Peace in Times of Need
ds: Patricia T. Holland shares some inspired “thoughts of peace in times of need” and bears witness that our Father in Heaven loves us.
President Johnson gives examples from her life on how to become "bound securely to the Savior" so that we can withstand the storms of life.

t: Time for the Savior at Christmas
ds: By following the prophet's invitation to make time for the Savior daily, we can experience the special spirit of Christmastime year-round.

t: The Need for a Mass Coming Together of Poor People and People of Faith in This Moment of Crisis
ds: An acclaimed advocate of the poor shares his vision for taking care of the needy.
"Take heed and go forth" means be humble and teachable in all aspects of life and know that God will provide the opportunities to learn.
BYU professor Gilbert W. Fellingham presents six rules for success in life from the perspective of a statistician and coach.

ds: We can build a “beloved community” daily by uniting with other Christians to face change together and invite all to come unto Christ.

t: The Dignity and Demeanor of Discipleship
ds: Rebecca L. Craven explores what the dignity and demeanor of discipleship look like. Standing as a witness of God means standing out.

t: Stay Connected: Making It Safely Home
ds: We must stay connected to the one true source of knowledge—Jesus Christ—so we can make it safely back home to our Father in Heaven.

t: BYU: Building a Community of Trust and Respect
ds: How inspired professors and faithful fellow students can help BYU flourish through an atmosphere of respect and trust.
Dale G. Renlund explains that lifelong conversion comes through determination to repeat the elements of the doctrine of Christ.

Identifying gospel methodologies to engage in efforts “left undone” by colleagues at other prominent institutions.

t: The Second Half of the Second Century of Brigham Young University
ds: Jeffrey R. Holland looks at where BYU is now and offers counsel about reaching for the university’s prophetic future.
Thoughts on the daunting but doable ways the university community can help ensure that BYU will “remain a unique university in all the world.”

t: Five Messages That All of God’s Children Need to Hear
ds: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf imparts hope, strength, and joy by sharing five messages he believes all of God’s children need to hear.

t: In Awe: The Astonishing Goodness of God
ds: John B. Bingham invites us to contemplate the goodness of God in awe by acting to believe, recording experiences, and seeking "thin" places.

t: Why Our Bodies Matter in a Digital World
ds: Amy Petersen Jensen shares examples of why our bodies matter in a digital world, citing from both personal and professional experiences.

t: “Yes, and . . .”: The Creative Art of Living
ds: Through her late husband's legacy, Lisa Valentine Clark teaches the importance of saying "yes, and . . . " in the creative art of living.

t: Vaulting to Greater Heights: Replacing Fear with Lasting Peace
ds: Melissa Western shares how she came to know the Savior, and her testimony that we can each replace our fear with lasting peace from Him.

Chris Crowe gives background on the YA novel and provides insights into how his understanding of genre influences his writing.

t: To Receive, to Covenant, and to Minister
ds: As we strive to actively receive and personally minister, we can create a home-court advantage for everyone around us.

t: Quinoa and Olive Trees: Strengthening the Lord’s Vineyard
ds: Rick Jellen uses his research on quinoa growth to discuss the allegory of the olive trees and the growing need for diversity in the Church.
Niwako Yamawaki shares her journey toward God, her experience as an immigrant, and her testimony of Christ's power to relieve suffering.
BYU Alumni Association president Karen Bybee shares how being connected for good with other BYU alumni is a blessing in a variety of ways.
Alyssa M. Baer, representative of her graduating class, explains why choosing who you will become is more important than what you will do.
A genuine BYU super graduate will recognize that true strength, resilience, durability, and adaptability comes from God.

t: A Tie That Binds Us All
ds: Marcus Roberts explains how music is a tie that binds us all together despite our differences. It also brings joy, peace, and inspiration.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong salutes graduates and tells their stories while celebrating BYU’s firm foundation of bedrock virtues, values, and principles.

t: “Look unto Me in Every Thought; Doubt Not, Fear Not”
ds: In our challenges, “we can, we should, and we must look unto the Savior in every thought to find every solution and to make every decision.”

t: Humility, Hope, and the Work of Becoming Educated
ds: Using lessons from America's history, Drew Faust teaches the role of humility and hope in both becoming educated and understanding death.

t: There Must Needs Be a Christ
ds: Kyle S. McKay shares why we need to embrace the plan of God and the doctrine of Christ; Christ can undo wrongs and provide healing.

t: His Sheep Still Hear His Voice
ds: Mark L. Pace explains how Christ's sheep still hear His voice by the power of the Holy Ghost. Daily gospel habits help us create change.

t: The Transformative Power of Faith and Art
ds: Janalee Emmer shares how both faith and art transform our hearts and foster empathy. Art can help us see the world from a new perspective.
Elder Gary E. Stevenson highlights the heavenly blessings we have received to help us with our divinely appointed responsibilities.

t: The Macroeconomic, Geopolitical, and Social Trends Defining Our World

t: “To Be Spiritually Minded Is Life and Peace”
ds: Elder José A. Teixeira teaches ways we can choose to be spiritually minded which leads to "life and peace" as well as hope.

t: “As Long as the World Shall Stand”

Scott D. Whiting teaches how to deepen discipleship through obedience, endurance, and service to God and our fellowmen and women.

t: Five Unexpected Things My Research Taught Me

Quentin L. Cook counsels the rising generation on how to live up to the expectations of their Heavenly parents in order to obtain joy.

t: Faith and Science: Symbiotic Pathways to Truth
ds: Dr. Jamie L. Jensen explains the symbiotic relationship between faith and science. The two can fit together without conflict.

t: What it Means to Be Educated
ds: Eboo Patel discusses how to be educated in today's interfaith world. It is necessary to understand others to bridge religious divides.

t: Harmony of Body and Spirit: A Key to Happiness
ds: Bishop Gérald Caussé teaches about the relationship between our bodies and spirits. Harmony between the two is the key to happiness.
Statistics professor Candace Berrett speaks about the earthly ministering angels that surround us each day.

t: The Education of the American Mind
ds: Melody Barnes speaks about the compatibility of science and faith while exploring what it means to educate the American mind.

t: Enduring and Trusting to the End
ds: Estela Marquez shares her life story to show how enduring and trusting to the end enables us to overcome life's challenges.

t: “Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve”
ds: Elder James B. Martino discusses the power that agency brings to our lives. You alone can choose "whom ye will serve."

t: The Process and Power of Hope
ds: Kevin J Worthen discusses hope in both a worldly and gospel context. Gospel-centered hope can purify us and prepare us for eternal life.

t: Faith and Courage to Move Forward
ds: Peggy S. Worthen reminds listeners that faith and courage are intimately connected. When faith flourishes, so does the courage to progress.
C. Shane Reese implores the faculty of Brigham Young University to be consumed with conviction as they work in today's unprecedented world.
Quentin L. Cook charges BYU faculty to persist in "well-doing" by lifting their and their students' vision and building faith in Christ.

t: How to Act While Being Acted Upon

t: Filling the World with Music of Faith

In a world that emphasizes identity, remember that above all else we are children of Heavenly Father. This is the most important group to identify with.
Marcus Roberts and The Modern Jazz Generation pair up with BYU professor Gregory Clark to perform music and discuss democracy through the lens of jazz.

t: Meekly Placing Our Total Trust in God
ds: As we encounter challenges in life, yoking ourselves with and meekly placing our total trust in God will allow us to reap the rewards of a faithful life.

Through a simple story, Peggy S. Worthen teaches that honesty and character are cultivated in ways that we might not expect.

t: How to Be Happy Now—and Forever

David Brooks, respected political and cultural commentator, teaches about the importance of character and persevering through life's challenges.

t: Harry Potter and the Five Gospel Truths

ds: The love and laws of God are inseparably connected. God's laws may not be popular in today's world, but they have been given for a reason.

The Real Value of a BYU Education

As we provide inspired, experiential learning to students, we must examine situations from many angles and in the light of the gospel.

Brent H. Nielson asks graduates to evaluate the condition of their hearts, for "where your heart is, there will your treasure be also."

Julie Crockett assures us that our uniqueness and divine individuality are only magnified as we work toward attaining Christlike attributes.

t: “Walk in the Meekness of My Spirit”

t: Our Identities at BYU and Beyond

ds: Learning a language gives you the incredible chance to enrich your mind, spirit, character, and ability to serve. But it takes work.

ds: We must intentionally seek the unspeakable gift of the Holy Ghost, which will instruct, guide, and testify to us.

ds: We are presented with many opportunities to let our light shine as a "standard for the nations."

ds: The Lord has promised that, even when we feel most lost and alone, even when those closest to us have forgotten us, He is aware of us.

t: “Where There Is No Vision, the People Perish”

t: The State of the University: Sound Spiritually, Academically, and Financially
ds: President Lee examines state of the BYU—deemed spiritually, academically, and financially sound—in light of a recent conference with the Board of Trustees.

t: “All Those Books, and the Spirit, Too!”
ds: Armed with books and the spirit, BYU faculty have the incredible potential to create Saints. We must be devoted to bettering their lives and the world.

t: Hopes and Dreams of an Even Better Brigham Young University

ds: Education can transform us into the divine beings we have the potential to become. By molding character in each of us, education can also mold our future.
George I. Cannon encourages students to remember the importance of living to make good memories that will bless them their whole lives.
To improve our eternal relationships, we must take sweet counsel from the Lord in prayer and with others in councils.
When we think of people in terms of "them and us," we fail to love individuals. The Savior shows us how to love His children rather than judge a label.

t: “Simon, I Have Somewhat to Say unto Thee”: Judgment and Condemnation in the Parables of Jesus
ds: Christ's parables taught about sin and forgiveness. Those who judge or condemn others for their sins have their own sins recalled to them.
Jesus Christ's Atonement exemplifies all of the divine attributes we are seeking. Truly, “in Him all things hold together.”
God loves all His children. With patience, we will have opportunities to serve the people of China, and one day to share the gospel there.
The Lord admonishes us to be one. This unity is seen in the councils of the Church as well as the blending of scholarship and faith at BYU.
Drawing parallels between our day and Book of Mormon times allows us to see how to fortify ourselves against the trials of our time.
President Lee unfolds the story and attributes of the U.S. Constitution and its significance for Latter-day Saints seeking to be good citizens.

t: Standards of Standard-Bearers of the Lord
ds: Our standards set us apart and enable us to be "standard-bearers" to the world of the Lord Jesus Christ and His Atonement.

t: What Will You Make Room for in Your Wagon?
ds: Many things in life compete for our attention, but we only have so much "room in our wagons." Prioritizing what really matters helps us get closer to God.
We should seek unity in individually developing ourselves by improving our minds, bodies, talents, health, and abilities.
The BYU educational, social, and spiritual experience is unique and not available to many. As a student here, make the most of your time and talents.
To bring down the power of heaven, we must learn the principle of waiting upon the Lord through real prayer, righteous living, and fervent listening.

t: Keeping an Open Mind about Things that Matter
sp: Janet G. Lee & Rex E. Lee
ds: When we judge too soon, we hurt others and we miss out on great opportunities. Especially when meeting other people, it is important to keep an open mind.
The home teacher is no less serviceable than the bishop, and the unsung heroes are just as important as the acclaimed and popular.

t: Meeting the Challenges of the Nineties
ds: Looking back on the eighties and forward to the nineties, Dallin H. Oaks identifies challenges that lay ahead for BYU in the new decade.

t: Mt. Everest Found: What BYU and Undergraduate Education Can Do For Each Other
ds: BYU is becoming an educational Mt. Everest, but it must not forget its unique purpose—to support the Church by offering the best in undergraduate education.

t: This Bequest of Wings Was But a Book
ds: It is time we re-evaluated what falls under the umbrella of scholarship for our faculty—because it is so much more than research at the expense of teaching.
We have many opportunities to conduct spiritual checkups on ourselves. Are we living up to the covenants we have made? Are our hearts pure?
We cannot sin without accepting the consequences, and sin always brings suffering. Sincere repentance is not easy, but it is possible.
BYU students must build a sure spiritual foundation so they can bravely and faithfully travel the right path after they leave the Y.
Many fruits come from obedience: peace, discipline, the capacity to work, love of service, confidence, and character.

t: Believing Christ: A Practical Approach to the Atonement
ds: Believing in Christ and believing Christ are two different things. Taking a practical approach to the Atonement can help us grow our faith.
Be eager to take advantage of the opportunities before you. Create a vision for your life and persevere in the attainment of it.
How do you confront seemingly impossible tasks? Everyone faces challenges, but without struggle we aren‘t able to appreciate life‘s goodness.
Elder Boyd K. Packer teaches that we should be grateful for the blessings of studying at BYU and to learn from those who teach and correct us.

t: A Still Voice of Perfect Mildness
ds: I have learned from five prophets—Presidents McKay, Smith, Lee, Kimball, and Benson—that the Lord speaks with a voice of mildness and love.
Neal A. Maxwell expounds on the nature of Christ and those who become His children through obeying His gospel and becoming like Him.

sp: Janet G. Lee & Rex E. Lee
ds: President and Sister Lee share how cancer taught them to find beauty in the storm. They learned to overcome and endure trials.
As we learn from past lessons and personal reflections, our resolutions can help us strengthen our future to become the people we want to be.
If we come unto Christ, His Atonement will make us clean and spotless. We can go home to live with God again, our deepest desire.

tp: Church Jesus Christ Latter Day Saints Mormons
ds: Is the Church found in chapels? Temples? Homes? Only if it is first in the hearts of its members. “The kingdom of God is within you.”
Despite intense opposition during some of the Church's history, the gospel has been busy unlocking the doors of nations and hearts worldwide.

t: Where Much Is Given: Some Thoughts on Appreciation
ds: President Lee reflects on how the untimely deaths of two close friends, plus his own battle with cancer, have given him a new appreciation for life.
Striving to be where Heavenly Father wants us to be will help us feel at home until the day comes when we return to our heavenly home.

tp: Church Jesus Christ Latter Day Saints Mormons
ds: I have had opportunity this summer to marvel at the time in which we live. I've been especially touched by the dedication of four special Church sites.
If we look to and study the life of Jesus Christ, we can learn how to become a leader in our families, church callings, and secular settings.
Elder Perry shares some of Brigham Young's teachings, which remind us to be obedient to God’s will, to be productive, and to dress modestly.

t: Our Mortal Body: A Sacred Gift
ds: Our mortal body is an eternal part of our soul. The way we use and treat our bodies has lasting physical, emotional, and spiritual implications.

t: That We May Prepare to Do Our Part
ds: Sometimes we're in the spotlight, and other times we serve quietly. If we play our part, no matter the role, God will be proud of us as we exit the stage.
Using the precious power to choose, we must choose to live by following the right rules, choosing discipline, and choosing the Master.
An education helps us to ask questions and find answers because we cannot truly understand the world until we bridge the gap to discovery.
Some commencement advice: consider the future, don't be too modest about your talents, and remember that the road to heaven is more work, but worth it.
The restoration of the gospel has unleashed a wonderful flood of light and knowledge about the nature of God and His children.
Financial worries, academic stress, and other struggles are inevitable for college students—we need not fear, because Christ is our Shepherd.
Hyrum Smith is an example of integrity, loyalty, and faith that we can strive to emulate. Remember, it is better to be trusted than be liked.
Christlike character is cultivated through our choices, not our circumstances or predispositions. We are always accountable for our actions.
Perfecting the Saints is part of the mission of the Church. Elder Jacob de Jager offers basic principles that help us as we strive to reach this lofty goal.

t: Filling the Measure of Your Creation
ds: God has a unique plan and a purpose for each of us, His creation. Finding and fulfilling that purpose will bring us wonderful peace.
Jesus Christ always submitted to the Father's will, no matter the cost. This difficult lesson of obedience is one we all must learn.
Each year presents an opportunity to set goals to be our best. As we set goals, let's try a little harder to be “more, Savior, like Thee.”
This unique Thanksgiving message reminds us to be grateful for our blessings through the covenant established with our father Abraham.
BYU is a unique university—it is guided by a modern-day prophet and spiritual values, while emphasizing both secular and sacred knowledge.
Our memories help shape us as we listen, learn, help, and serve others, and we will carry our memories with us through life.

t: At Their Most Enlightened and Alert
ds: George Washington, one of the "wise men" the Lord raised up to lead the US, is commemorated. Our leaders reflect our own enlightened state.

t: Be Renewed in the Spirit of your Mind
ds: We can't fight our external battles by waging internal wars. Positive thinking must continually renew our mind—we must be our own best friend.

t: The Authority of Personality, Competence, and Character
ds: There are many in positions of authority, but those with personality, competence, character, and integrity posses real authority.
To hear the voice of God, we must learn to listen to His disciples and to the Spirit. This listening requires prayer, study, righteous living, and service.
Jeffrey R. Holland expresses the necessity of a school in Zion and discusses how BYU students and faculty can fulfill its unique mission.
To serve and "love thy neighbor" is the essence of joy and will prepare us to meet God. All of us can do something, and most of us more than we are doing.

The history of BYU is built on the stories of inspiring individuals who sacrificed their time and means. Aunt Carrie Harman’s story is no different. She set an example for all of how the application of our education unlocks opportunities and gives us a greater commitment to responsibility.

t: One Man Can Make a Difference
ds: A mission president helps a discouraged missionary recognize one man can make a difference by reminding him of the Savior.
The relationship between religion and the United States constitution has an interesting and complicated history with important implications.
Lessons from the experience with the woman taken in adultery shows how Christ was the master teacher, full of love, compassion, and testimony.

t: Study, Faith, and the Book of Mormon
ds: John W. Welch gives examples of different ways many scholars learn from the Book of Mormon by both methods of study and of faith.
We all experience life's peaks and valleys—spiritual highs and lows. How can we remain at the top and not slide into spiritual darkness?
Intelligence and knowledge are only stepping-stones to wisdom and understanding, which help us use our learning to bless others.
As we become the most worthy versions of ourselves and strive to lift others, the Lord will be able to use us to build His kingdom.
The gospel is “simply beautiful and beautifully simple.” Understanding the simplicity of the first gospel principles helps us to live righteously.
We are here in this university of mortality to learn eternal values. Some courses might include self-worth, morality, integrity, and hard work.
Jeffrey R. Holland discusses the sanctity of chastity and physical intimacy. The power of souls, symbols, and sacraments is gifted from God.
Although the world's path may seem easier, the sanctifying and refining tears that come from a life of discipleship "give way to eternal tears of joy."
Our life is like a stream—many other streams have fed and influenced us. Are you heading toward flowing into the fountain of living water?
The law of chastity is a principle of eternal significance. Take seriously this counsel to avoid sin, and to use the blessings of repentance when needed.
God's plan includes agency, the freedom to choose. That cannot be taken away, but our freedom, or ability to act on our choices, can.
The Constitution was written through divine inspiration. We are blessed by our freedoms and are responsible for ensuring liberty continues.
Patricia Holland reminds students that often fear is our greatest enemy. As we follow the scriptural admonition to "fear not," our faith is magnified.

t: “Who We Are and What God Expects Us to Do”
ds: BYU is founded on inspiring tradition that, when understood and honored, helps us fulfill the lofty mission of this university.
Now is the time to determine to keep the commandments of God. Now is the time to repent, to create faithful families, and to fulfill our purpose.
James E. Faust discusses the profound legacy of Brigham Young University, emphasizing the gospel and the devotion of students and faculty.
Like Job, BYU holds fast to integrity—uniting faithful citizenship, strong teaching, and solid scholarship to build wisdom and understanding.

t: “Whence Then Cometh Wisdom? And Where Is the Place of Understanding?”
ds: J. Elliot Cameron honors the devotion of early Saints, inviting those at BYU to foster great learning and strive to be stewards of Christ.

t: Some Lessons I Learned from Living Sixty Years
ds: Elder Dean L. Larsen shares profound lessons with BYU students about living life and the gospel gleaned from his years of experience.

t: Some Observations on the Law of the Harvest

ds: If we never experienced sadness, then we would never experience joy. Adversity is part of God's plan of happiness.
As children of God, there is much for us to learn. By being teachable, we can learn of Heavenly Father's love for us and edify each other.
Marvin J. Ashton's message is take up your cross. Take yourself the way you are and lift yourself in the direction of the better.
One of the most magnificent creations of God is the remarkably complex human body, which ought to be an object of appreciation and respect.
To have dependable staying power in your life, subscribe to basic principles, consistently do your best, and choose character over reputation.
What does it mean to be a woman of faith? Patricia Holland addresses this topic in her BYU address, encouraging women to recognize their divine identity.
True greatness is not a one-time achievement: it requires many correct, everyday choices between good and evil.

t: Your Inheritance: Secure or in Jeopardy?
ds: The choices we make in this life determine our eternal inheritance. To become heirs of God, we must choose to obey the commandments He has given us.

t: The Church in the British Isles 1837-1987
ds: Gordon B. Hinckley gives an inspiring history of the Church in the British Isles, from the Restoration to his own mission and on into the present.

t: The Church in the British Isles Symposium: Plenary Session
ds: The history of the Church in England and the British Isles is a rich legacy of courageous, faithful pioneers who endured incredible trials.
Sister Holland offers some advice for the modern woman who, exhausted by others' expectations, needs help find her inner self and rejuvenate her soul.

t: The Bitter Cup and the Bloody Baptism
ds: Jesus Christ and His disciples know what it means to stand firm for the "duration of the war" - to drink the bitter cup in the battle between good and evil.

We are on a journey, going home. We must search for truth and seek the companionship of the Holy Ghost to guide this journey.
The world equates meekness to weakness, but that is not true. Only the meek and lowly in heart are prepared to serve in the Lord's vineyard.

t: Great Answers to the Great Question
ds: Through the witness of the Book of Mormon and prophetic revelation, the gospel offers great answers to age-old questions of the soul.
How can we have the kind of simple, pure, untroubled faith to move mountains and bring peace? Build and nurture faith on a solid foundation.
The Constitution of the United States is divinely inspired. We ought to learn of it, to be grateful for it, and to defend it.

sp: Jeffrey R. Holland & Patricia T. Holland
ds: What does it mean to be a Mormon? When the pressure mounts to break our standards, will we be true? What values define our character?

t: I’ll Go, I’ll Do, I’ll Be: Three Steps Toward A Monumental Life
ds: To create a strong, inspiring, and monumental life, one must learn to go, do, and be all that the Lord requires and asks of us.
In making bricks, the children of Israel needed straw to hold together and strengthen the building material. Here are some examples of spiritual straw.

t: Our Talents—A Choice Gift of God
ds: As we move toward eternal progression, we must develop our God-given talents so that our capacity to serve God and our fellow man can and will increase.
In this BYU community of students and Saints, let us foster an environment of fellowship as we learn, work, and serve together.

t: The Stick of Joseph and the Stick of Judah
ds: Bruce L. Brown shares insights that demonstrate the importance of studying and appreciating the prophecies in the Bible, or the "stick of Judah."
Two different types of fear are discussed: the fear of sin because of punishment and the fear of sin because it prevents being with God.

t: We Thank Thee, O God, for a Prophet
ds: I testify to the truth of this work and of living prophets. God calls a prophet to reveal His truth, to His children, in His time.
Divorce is, sadly, all too common. Elder Burton's speech focuses on the great love story of Adam and Eve and how to keep your marriage strong.

t: The Prince of Peace: “Peace I Give unto You”
ds: When tragedy strikes, turn to God in faith—and to the people He has placed in your life. Through trust, service, and love, you will find lasting peace.

t: A Return to Full Belief in God
ds: George P. Lee calls for an individual and worldwide return to full belief in God and His gospel, as opposed to half-believing and counterfeit faith.

Time is our royal inheritance as children of promise, and the way we spend or invest it determines our own reward and the inheritance of others.

t: Building the Kingdom from a Firm Foundation
ds: Women of the Church come from all walks of life, but each woman, when her foundation is strong in Christ, builds the Kingdom of God in her own unique way.

t: Oh, Lord, Keep My Rudder True
ds: Whether standing for the gospel, our standards, or a brother, will we be true? Where does our loyalty lie, and how do we show it?

t: “Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve”

t: Nailing Our Colors to the Mast

tp: Church Jesus Christ Latter Day Saints Mormons

Spiritual experiences are real, and commandments of the Lord are given so we can achieve spiritual progress.

t: The Contemplation of Beauty: An Avenue to Communication with the Lord

Family relationships are precious. We should tell our families we love them, help them feel safe, and emulate scriptural examples.

t: “Rejoice in Christ Jesus, and Have No Confidence in the Flesh”
ds: As we choose to follow the Savior, and have no confidence in the contrary messages of the world, we will understand our great potential in His eternal plan.
Our life is a book made up of chapters in which we learn important lessons, including how to best prioritize the Lord and his commandments.

t: The Testament of Bruce R. McConkie
ds: Elder John K. Carmack pays tribute to the testimony of the late Elder Bruce R. McConkie, who "taught as one having authority" and bore witness of Christ.

t: Women, Feminism, and the Blessings of the Gospel
ds: In an age of feminism, know that men and women have unique natures and roles, but neither are superior. Both sexes must develop their minds and hearts.
Building our understanding is like building a temple: we must follow a plan from Heavenly Father, line upon line and precept upon precept.
Repentance includes admitting, reconciling, and forsaking the sin. While not easy, it's possible through the atonement of our loving Savior.

t: The Doctrine and Covenants—A Scripture for All Seasons
ds: The Doctrine and Covenants not only teaches us Church doctrine but also how to receive personal revelation. Do you treasure the D&C?
Memory has power to influence your mood, your view of the world, your testimony and scriptural understanding, and your personal connections.
With an eternal perspective, God will help you—our granddaughters, and all women—fulfill your divine missions in the family, the Church, and the world.

t: The Peaceable Things of the Kingdom
ds: Achieving perfection is a lifelong endeavor, and to prevail we must be patient with ourselves, trust God, and give of ourselves.

sp: Jeffrey R. Holland & Patricia T. Holland
ds: Jeffrey and Patricia Holland share the lessons they have learned in their marriage, with great counsel for developing healthy relationships.

None of us can be immune from life‘s trials. But if we learn to endure our struggles well, they will be turned into blessings in eternity.

t: Why a Savior Is Necessary, and Why Only Jesus Christ Could Qualify
ds: In living the gospel, we must understand why a Savior is necessary for our physical and spiritual salvation. He is the greatest gift.

t: Future Challenges for an International Church
ds: Elder Ballard shares how the Church is growing on an international scene and urges members to follow the counsel of the prophet to share the gospel.
There are specific teachings and friends we should remember who are high in their personal ranking because of the values they exemplify.

t: Joseph Smith Translation: The Doctrinal Restoration
ds: Elder McConkie bears testimony of the truth and usefulness of revealed scripture, including the Joseph Smith Translation of the Bible.

t: Whatever We Ought to Be, We Better Be Becoming
sp: Helen Wells & Robert E. Wells & Sharlene Wells
ds: Sharlene Wells, daughter of Robert E. Wells, speaks with her parents at a fireside as reigning Miss America and shares her story of becoming.

Although the world may move further away from moral traditions, we must preserve the culture of the gospel and forsake incorrect traditions.

t: Begin with the End in Mind
ds: When we die, what do we want to have defined our lives? For Russell M. Nelson, it is service to mankind, family, and faith in God.
By striving for personal worthiness, being hungry to learn, and drinking of living water, we can avoid many pitfalls of our day and find success and joy.

sp: Jeffrey R. Holland & Patricia T. Holland
ds: Honesty, education, sacrifice, and faith are among the unique characteristics that make up Zion–and we can make Zion right here at BYU.

Your free agency is a gift from God and can save you from being tied down by procrastination, bad habits, and debilitating excuses.

t: “Where the Spirit of the Lord Is, There Is Liberty”
ds: Liberty comes from following Christ and must be defended, not only on wartorn battlefields, but in our everyday actions against the evils of the world.
No matter how complicated your trials, how dark your sins, or how overwhelming the challenges you face, in Christ there is always hope.
Life is a struggle. Major decisions face all of you. But they are solvable and you will pass through them successfully if you trust in the Lord.
In life's opportunities for giving and getting, let us be more concerned with giving. Nothing worth getting comes without work and sacrifice.
As members of Christ’s church, we should be among them that love Him by following His instructions and remembering our worth.
Derek A. Cuthbert discusses the futility of fear by pointing out that whether it be key to overcoming any kind of fear is to have great faith.
We all sin, but we don't have to live with those burdens forever. Through repentance, we can be made clean through the Atonement of Christ.

t: Guidance: Ongoing Guidance Is Needed for All
ds: In order to accomplish the things we truly desire, we need to follow some basic principles to receive guidance from the Lord.

Cultivate a relationship with your Heavenly Father, and seek His guidance as you make important decisions. He will lead, protect, and help you.

t: Love Is Life and Life Hath Immortality
ds: Love of all kinds is life and is meant to be eternal. As we seek to create loving relationships, we will change the world forever.
No matter what trials and tribulations come our way, we must develop the faith to be able to say to our Heavenly Father, "Thy will be done."
Using the tagline, "spiritual is as spiritual does," Mary Ellen Edmunds reminds us that spirituality is determined by the steps we take to develop it.

t: A Robe, a Ring, and a Fatted Calf
ds: The story of the prodigal son testifies that no matter the severity our sins, there is always a way back to light, peace, and eternal life.
Optimism leads to hope, which leads to faith. If we can come to remember the glorious things we once knew, our faith can be limitless as walking on water.

t: What Think Ye of Salvation by Grace?
ds: We will not be saved by our works, but Christ’s grace does not absolve us from effort. True faith in Jesus Christ requires action.

t: The Atonement and Our Part in It
ds: Elder A. Theodore Tuttle discusses the Atonement and our part in it. We must take important steps to fully access the Savior's Atonement.
Future world and Church leaders must learn early to weigh decisions, use common sense, and invest in the future - in other words, to think straight.

t: Some Glances at the Past at Thanksgiving Time
ds: Robert J. Smith gives us some glances at the past that help us to be more thankful for the present and to act better in the future.

t: Souls Aflame: The Prayer Heritage of the Latter-day Saints
ds: Our theology is derived from prayer—we pray to God whom we know, and we must do so with our whole souls, with faith, sincerity, and love.

The invitation to follow the Savior is an invitation to open our hearts. If we learnt o love as He does, we will be blessed with success in our missionary efforts.

t: If I Were You, What Would I Do?
ds: Students are encouraged to take advantage of their opportunities at BYU with a lighthearted poem, “If I Were You, What Would I Do?”

sp: Jeffrey R. Holland & Patricia T. Holland
ds: The root of disciple is found in discipline. We need the discipline to keep high standards, to take advantage of our opportunities, and to love one another.
Learn to love yourself as God does, for you have infinite value and potential. Elder Faust suggests essentials to keep a healthy self-esteem.
Good managers produce personal gain and rely on the wisdom of the world, but great leaders build the Lord's kingdom. Leadership relies on God.

t: Parallel Prophets: Paul and Joseph Smith
ds: Richard Anderson shares how Paul and Joseph Smith are similar. Both received revelation, demonstrated service, and were ultimately martyred.

Agency is central to the Plan of Salvation. Using it to follow God's commandments gives us true independence and power over our destiny.
Each of us is called to be a torchbearer for the Lord. To carry His light bright and strong, we need the virtues of a loving, diligent servant.

t: Christianity and the Hope of the Future
ds: The sordid and complicated history of Christianity is clear evidence that God's church needs the guiding hand of continuous revelation.

t: “That Ye May Be Filled with Love”
ds: Hartman Rector Jr. teaches that in order to serve effectively, we need to learn to love others selflessly and unconditionally, as He loves us.

Not all experiences in life will be easy or fun, but we can find joy regardless of our circumstances. Even when faced with a frustrating or discouraging challenge, we can choose to enjoy it and make the most of what we have been given.
Goals help us to determine where we are going and how to get there. We should strive diligently toward worthy, eternal goals.
Taking accountability for our actions and letting others take accountability for theirs is essential to the plan of salvation.
No matter how much the world changes, we can succeed in discovering truth—in both secular and spiritual matters—if we are willing to work for it.
In her BYU Women's Conference address, Patricia T. Holland teaches that peace comes as we love each other without judgment, comparison, or pettiness.
With the literary imagery of “the frost” and “the thaw,” Arthur Henry King warns against warring between sexes. Men and women need one another.

t: “Try the Virtue of the Word of God”
ds: The word of God is more powerful than sword or any other force. When it seems that nothing else is able, God's word has the power to heal and change us.

t: “Deep Roots Are Not Reached by the Frost”
ds: Children share many parallels with trees and plants: they have great potential for growth, and they need support to reach that potential.

t: President Wilford Woodruff and Thoughts for Youth
ds: President Wilford Woodruff, a faithful leader in the Church in its very early days, left some insights for the youth that are relevant today.

t: Our Faith Is Centered on the Living Christ
tp: Church Jesus Christ Latter Day Saints Mormons
ds: Our Church, faith, and gospel have Jesus Christ for their foundation. The scriptures and the lives of latter-day prophets testify of Him.

t: However Long and Hard the Road
sp: Jeffrey R. Holland & Patricia T. Holland
ds: However long and hard the road, we must be willing to endure with perseverance until we can claim sweet victory.
Robert Backman reminds us that there are many wonders yet to come. The upcoming generation has a responsibility to create and bring them forth.
With the Plan of Salvation, a knowledge of who we are, and a testimony of the gospel, we have a fuller understanding of life.
As we seek the influence of the Holy Ghost, we will have the gift of knowing how to balance our time and what to do when we face important decisions.
What does it mean to be born again? Baptism becomes effective through the Atonement of Jesus Christ and brings us into His family.
Romantic love is pure, sacred, and central to the gospel. It is because of, not in spite of, that fact that we must treat it carefully.
God has said that every blessing is predicated upon obedience to a law. As we consistently choose obedience, we also choose the rewards for obedience.

t: Dedication of the John Taylor Building
ds: We honor the third president of the Church, John Taylor, a man of courage and faith. This new building of learning reminds us of his example.

t: “A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defense”
sp: Jeffrey R. Holland & Patricia T. Holland
ds: At BYU, we are a community of love and have a duty to look after one another, to be a friend, and to protect honor and integrity.
Meekness does not oppose boldness. It means to speak up without speaking down. It means to depend upon the Lord. It means to become like the Savior.
To continue learning, we must experience the smorgasbords of life rather than only the hamburgers. Leave your comfort zone and explore.
Life may seem unfair and unsatisfactory to the lonely and misunderstood, but purpose can be found through faith, repentance, obedience, and service.
By putting on the spiritual armor of God, we can protect ourselves from Satan's efforts to cut us off from the Holy Ghost and His divine influence.

t: Differences . . . “Allow All Men the Same Privilege”
ds: Differences in religion, personality, and nationality can lead us to criticize others, but we should be tolerant and love everyone.
Sacrifice is the source of love. To truly love someone else or the Lord, we must be willing to sacrifice and pay whatever price is necessary.
How often do we ask ourselves "Can God trust me?" Trust involves accepting what we do not understand, even when we are not certain of the outcome.
Never will our time or efforts be better rewarded than when they are spent in service and kindness. This kind of investing for eternity should be our aim.
The aim of education is so much more than getting a job. Education has the capacity to shape our character—a blessing that cannot be replaced.

t: Becoming Men and Women of Principle
ds: Adrian Van Mondfrans explains how to become men and women of principle. There are gospel formulas we can follow to become better.
Spiritual leprosy, like physical leprosy, can cause us to lose feeling. Yet, like physical illness, we can be healed through courage and the help of Christ.
Drawing parallels between the olive press and the events in Gethsemane, Truman G. Madsen invites us to reflect on Christ's atoning sacrifice.
Reflecting on his upbringing, Elder Dunn shares stories of his community heritage and invites us to embrace our common spiritual heritage.
To gain learning and understanding, we must use the proper equipment. Both rational thought and spiritual revelation are necessary for our progression.
When money becomes our god, we are poor. One of life’s great lessons is that what we do with what we have is more important than what we have.
Much less known than the economic law of decreasing returns is the spiritual law of increasing returns. Working and waiting are worth the blessings.
If you can cultivate a creative mind in setting and working toward worthy goals, your horizons will expand and your amazing potential will be within reach.
When we speak of our relationship with deity, it is important to remember the closeness and love that God feels for us, yet the reverence we owe Him.
We will all experience trials. Hard times do not make us courageous; the decisions we make in everyday situations shape our character.
Like flaxen threads, seemingly insignificant habits build up in our lives and become impenetrable. Make wise choices; actions may become habits.

sp: Jeffrey R. Holland & Patricia T. Holland
ds: Christ overcame temptation for appetite, glory, and wealth. His way was inconvenient, and ours will be too if we truly follow Him.
Elder Jager lists just some of the blessings we receive by being part of BYU. Count your blessings frequently, and strive to live up to them.
Richard H. Cracroft amusingly discusses the value of humor. Laughter is a gift from God, as is the talent of making others laugh.

t: “This Is the Way; and There Is None Other Way”
ds: Christ is the only way to eternal life. To become like Him, we must keep His commandments. We need good friends and to be a good friend.
We are responsible to learn of and become witnesses of Jesus Christ. As we do, we positively influence our posterity and those around us.
We are often filled with the desire to make a difference in the world. In order to have the impact we want, however, we must prepare spiritually.

t: Faith in the Lord Jesus Christ
ds: Faith in the Lord is more than just a passive feeling. True faith is a principle of action and sacrifice, and it brings about miracles.

Almost all of the problems in our lives, our families, and our communities could be solved if we would simply replace our selfishness with selflessness. With selflessness we demonstrate our true relationship and intimacy with the Savior. It is the link that binds together the family of God.
The missionary experiences of Elder LeGrand Richards testify that the doctrines of the gospel of Jesus Christ speak for themselves.
Revelation serves many purposes necessary and beneficial: it testifies, prophesies, comforts, uplifts, informs, restrains, confirms, and impels.
When the storms of life test our faith, we must be prepared. As a sturdy tree, be grounded, rooted, established, and settled in Jesus Christ.

sp: Jeffrey R. Holland & Patricia T. Holland
ds: President Holland asks students to appreciate the privilege of being at BYU by contributing to its aims of virtus, virtue, and veritas, truth.
If we strive to experience excellence and endure here on earth, we will build character that will last throughout the eternities.
It is each of our responsibility to preserve generational testimony by teaching truth to our children and strengthening our families.
Brigham Young's admonition to the Saints to bring in the pioneers suffering on the plains was a reminder to us all: we are our Brother’s Keeper.

t: Walking in the Footsteps of Jesus
ds: As we seek to walk in the footsteps of Jesus, we need to understand Him better. Ivan J. Barrett offers insights into the character of Christ.
Are we sometimes guilty of portraying a righteous appearance but lacking true spiritual substance? The essence of real godliness is explored.
It is not enough to be casually reading the scriptures; we need to be using the scriptures to learn the gospel thoroughly and learn how to live it.
Gospel learning comes by the process of reason and revelation. We must take care to learn by the Holy Ghost rather than be deceived by Satan.
The purpose of life is using our talents to benefit others. Our spiritual gifts are used to build the kingdom of God if we choose to improve and serve.
The scriptures teach that the key to life eternal is to know God and His Son. What pride, fear, or sin is stopping us from truly coming to know Him?
Everyone is involved in the same business: the business of being. To become the best disciples that we can be, we must increase in dedication to Christ.
As we strive to take His name upon us and honor our sacrament covenants every day of the week, we will draw closer to Christ and serve and love as He does.

t: Ten Keys to Successful Dating and Marriage Relationships
ds: Marriage is key for our exaltation, but successful marriages do not come without hard work. Elder Pinnock offers ten suggestions for happier marriages.

t: Prepare Yourselves for the Great Day of the Lord
ds: No one knows the great day of the Lord's Second Coming, but we do know the signs. More importantly, we know how to prepare and therefore need not fear.
The prophet has directed us to engage in missionary work and share the gospel. Will you listen to his voice and accept the challenge?

t: “A Love of God and of All Men”
ds: With Southeast Asian refugees as beautiful examples, Elder Hanks shares what it means to truly love our neighbor by feeding the body, mind, and soul.
Don't become so engrossed in one issue or area of your life that you can't have balance. Be well-rounded, excel, and have a sense of humor.
Arthur Henry King points to classic passages of Shakespeare's work to show that Shakespeare and the gospel share some important themes in common.
Remembering that others watch you, and that you represent your faith, will help you practice courtesy and strive to do your best.
Our light will shine and we will influence the world for good as we respect the agency of others and have pure intentions.
The Creation, the Fall, and the Atonement are the foundations of salvation. As we understand them better, we can live to gain eternal life.
Hartman Rector Jr. teaches that it is our responsibility to fulfill Malachi's promise and turn hearts to their roots and branches.
Decisions determine our actions, our habits, our character, and our destiny. Are you making decisions that will help you end up where you want to go?
As we acquire new skills and hobbies, grow in intellect, and learn to unleash priesthood power in our homes, we can change our divine potential.
May we determine this year to live "in the world," to be a part of it, to set the standard and example that we have learned.
This Christmas, remember the best gifts are given when the giver feels for the receiver, gives freely, and counts the sacrifice as a bargain.

t: “By Their Fruits Ye Shall Know Them”
ds: The fruits of a Christlike life are loving, serving, and giving. May we all strive to better emulate Him this Christmas season.

t: Thanks for the Things that Count
ds: W. Rolfe Kerr encourages us to take a moment to express gratitude for the things that count in life, especially our friends, our freedoms, and our families.
We ought to cultivate a spirit of thanksgiving for the many blessings we have in the gospel—including the commandments, which are evidence of God's love.

t: Installation of and Charge to the President

ds: As you move through your mortal journey, you must issue a proclamation to those around you. Share and declare your beliefs with pride.
As we base our behavior on gospel concepts, we will find that our lives are much richer than those that are founded in the faulty concepts of men.

t: Abide in the Light of the Gospel
ds: We must be wary of spiritual blindness, allowing the gospel to leave our lives. If we abide in the light God offers us, we will never be lost.
The true believers in Christ are not just tourists, but natives in the kingdom of God. They love Him and follow Him whole-heartedly.
We are the covenant people of God, and as such, we have a responsibility to live and share the gospel as we strive to fulfill His prophecies.
The priesthood, the presence of the Holy Ghost, our temple covenants—these are heavenly powers that bless our lives when we live the gospel.
Make the most of your BYU education. Aquire not only an academic literacy but a spiritual one that will bless your family and the world.
D. Arthur Haycock gives a tribute to President and Sister Kimball. They are kind, courageous, and obedient to the Lord.
The key to our redemption is Christ's Atonement and the temple, along with the saving ordinances performed there for the living and the dead.
You are the hope of tomorrow. Embrace friendship, responsibility, and love to build strong families through faith and education.

sp: Jeffrey R. Holland & Patricia T. Holland
ds: Understanding BYU’s mission goes beyond standards—it means taking your education seriously and staying true to your faith.
The strength of a university comes from uniting faith and scholarship through charity, humility, and shared responsibility.

t: Ten Characteristics of an Educated Person
ds: Education is vital both here on earth and into the eternities. Elder Pinnock gives characteristics of educated persons and how they make the world better.

t: The Heritage of Our Summer Holidays
ds: As we celebrate the various summer holidays, we must remember the heritage they commemorate and determine to preserve the gifts we’ve been given.
“On my honor” is the rule by which every Latter-day Saint must govern their life. Living with honor brings the light of truth into our lives.
The legacy of a name gives the bearer the responsibility to honor it. We have been blessed with not only a family name, but the name of Christ.

t: On Making Revelation a Personal Reality
ds: You can make revelation a personal reality as you search the scriptures, commune with the Father, and live in keeping with divine commandments.
Widely-circulated heresies can act as stumbling blocks for LDS church members. Seek out a knowledge of true doctrine, and live by it.

t: Some Thoughts on Goal Setting, Objectives, and Measurements
ds: We often set quantitative goals as we strive for improvement, but we must not to let check-mark goals take us away from true, qualitative progression.
To master the "art of living" and be happy, we must be willing to do what will bring us happiness—live the commandments of God.

t: In This Time of Complexity and Challenge
ds: In this increasingly secular world, faith in God will bless you through. Hold on to Him through the complexity and challenges of life.
When we are converted to Christ, we are united as a Church. Elder Dunn suggests ways we can feel the healing, uniting Spirit in our lives.
Strive to live worthy of the blessings you were given in your patriarchal blessings. Your spiritual lineage is a heritage of faith and trust.
A teacher's attitude has far-reaching effects on students. Learn to admit, with humility, faith, and love, what you know—and what you don't.
Trouble will come, but discouragement doesn't have to. If we prepare ourselves through patient and faithful discipleship, we‘ll get through.
God always answers our prayers but often not in the way or timeframe we would like. As we exercise patience and faith, our relationship with Him will grow.

t: Fourteen Fundamentals in Following the Prophet
ds: We can show our devotion to the Lord as we follow counsel given through His servant, the prophet. We will be blessed as we heed this counsel.
The Osmond family bear their testimonies, and Elder Dunn offers this message: press forward, for you never know what good your effort can do.
Through ordinances, the power of God is made manifest in our lives. Be faithful to gospel covenants and ordinances, and you will be happy.
Exemplary Womanhood Award winner and Church curator Florence S. Jacobsen shares Church artifacts that demonstrate our history and heritage as Saints.
As we honor our parents through righteous and respectful living, we feel of their love and receive blessings from following their counsel.
Don't abandon sound economic principles: stay out of unnecessary debt, use a budget, and set yourselves up for financial peace of mind.
There are many talents worth pursuing, but none that surpass the talent of spirituality. Elder Rector gives suggestions to help us improve this talent.

t: Tithing: A Law of Peace and Security
ds: It is a privilege to obey the law of tithing. Through it, the Lord blesses the Church with growth and individuals with greater faith and capacity for good.
Having patience with ourselves and our circumstances will bring us closer to God and increase our love, humility, and willingness to submit to Him.
Missionary work allows us to reap the full blessings and joy of the gospel as we share that joy with others. It is at the heart of the Lord's plan.
Gordon B. Hinckley shares his testimony of the prophet Joseph Smith. The most important evidence of his calling is the witness of the Spirit.
J. Richard Clarke expounds on how consecration, concentration, conscience, and conquest lead us down "the royal road to happiness."
The simple eternal truth of the gospel is that Jesus Christ is our Redeemer and has restored His Church to the earth to help us return to Him.

t: A Man Must Be Called of God
ds: The scriptures teach that prophets and apostles, called by God, are the foundation of the Church, with Christ as the chief cornerstone.
Elder Simpson shares touching missionary experiences among people in China and the Soviet Bloc. He testifies that one day, the Lord will be able to send the gospel to all people and nations.
The spirit of BYU and its students is special. Much of that uniqueness comes from your character and integrity.
As we face the challenges of living the gospel, we may often ask ourselves, "Is it worth it?" The blessings of eternal life ARE worth it.

t: The Formula for Success at BYU
ds: Many things have changed at BYU over the years, but not its formula for success: being worthy, seeking learning, working hard, and helping others.

t: We Never Know Where Walking in His Steps Will Lead
ds: Walking in the steps of the Savior is not easy, but it will bring you experiences and growth that you will be forever grateful for.
John S. Staley explores facets of the fullness of the gospel that have blessed his life since his conversion to the Church of Jesus Christ.
L. Tom Perry delivers a patriotic fireside address recounting the history of America and the great gifts that its founding has brought.

t: A Word to You: Generation of Destiny!
ds: Time is a resource and gift given to us from God. In our mission to use time wisely, we must remember that it is never too late to make important decisions. These decisions are how we we enter into life—eternal life.

t: The Dangers of Extremism, Fanaticism, and Skepticism
ds: Donald Q. Cannon teaches that we need to balance study and faith, and that all virtues can become vices in the realm of extremism.

t: The Sacred Way to Eternal Life Is to Love God First
ds: The way to the kingdom of God is to love God first. We must love and serve Him above money, appetites, and other temporary priorities.
There are many "necessities of living" here in mortality: thoughts, ideas, words, character traits, and acts to aid us in becoming who we need to be.
Only the Creator can establish a true value system and determine what is right and wrong. Our job is to live by His principles to obtain His blessings.
We are surrounded by a cloud of witnesses of Jesus Christ. Elder Asay gives counsel on how to make sure we are honest disciples of Christ.
Discovering your mission in life is a daunting, but not impossible task. If you trust Him and have the courage to act, God will guide and shape your life.
Because the gospel has been restored, and because we are blessed to know about it, we have a solemn responsibility to live according to it.

t: Wife and Mother: A Valid Career
ds: Today's world values money and prestige. Seek education and marketability, but never forget to respect the sacred importance of family.

t: We Need Not Fear His Coming
ds: The Second Coming will bring judgment on the wicked. By living God's commandments, we can look forward to that day with joy and without fear.
God bless us that we may have the good sense to take the Holy Spirit as our guide and accomplish the purpose for which this life was given to us.
As a newly called apostle and special witness of Jesus Christ, James E. Faust shares his testimony of the divinity and works of the Savior.
Ezra Taft Benson teaches that Christ grew in wisdom, stature, and favor with God and man. We can follow in His steps by prioritizing.
As a Church, we ought to have charity, which is the pure love of Christ, reflected in every word, act, and deed, setting a true example for the world.

t: “Mirror, Mirror, on the Wall”: A Look at the “Me Decade”
ds: Our greatest fulfillment and joy, the focus of each new decade, is not to be found in the mirror. It is found by losing ourselves in service to others.
George P. Lee encourages us to, as the Navajo saying admonishes, "walk in beauty." Such beauty comes from within—from kind, uplifting, righteous thoughts.
When it comes to race and color, we are all Heavenly Father's children and He loves us equally. There is nor room for prejudice among God's children.
The BYU students who are going forth to serve the world cannot forget that they represent the university and the Church in word and deed.
Avoid the trap of vanity and hypocrisy. Instead of worrying about how you seem to others, be the kind of person you know you can and should be.

t: Love Is Not Blind: Some Thoughts for College Students on Faith and Ambiguity
ds: We face ambiguity when reality does not meet the ideal. Faith and ambiguity are both possible once we learn that to God, love is not blind, but bound.
Prophecies, visions, and dreams may take different forms for you. Take time for teaching the gospel, for contemplation, and for chasing worthy dreams.
We believe in the gift of prophecy. We see today the fulfillment of prophecies from long ago, and they give us faith to follow our living prophets now.
Where will you be a millennia from now? If you heed the voice of the prophet and follow his guidance, you will not go astray.
The "uttermost part" of the earth is not only your campus, but your mission field. Prepare to help the gospel to reach all of God's children.
As we face the challenges of today, the doctrine of foreordination teaches that God knows all things, and plans for each of us to succeed.
When school, the weather, or life in general leaves you in a state of the "blahs," reach up. Reach out. Learn. And never, never give up.
God did not go to the trouble of creating the earth and creating us in his own image for us to fail. Our motivations will determine our life's success.
Abiding by the standards at BYU is a sign of honor. It shows that when you sign an agreement to do something, you intend to do it.
Where much is given, much is expected, not only in scholastic achievement and developing talents but also in conduct and the way we present ourselves.

t: Joseph Smith: A Revealer of Christ
ds: Joseph Smith's most important contribution as a revealer and the Prophet of the Restoration is his testimony of the Lord Jesus Christ.

t: Joseph Smith Lecture 7: Doctrinal Development and the Nauvoo Era
ds: Truman Madsen on the lessons learned and taught by Joseph Smith in Nauvoo while the Prophet directed the saints in building the temple.

t: Joseph Smith Lecture 8: The Last Months and Martyrdom
ds: Truman Madsen covers the martyrdom of Joseph Smith and the last few months of the Prophet’s life before adding his personal testimony.

t: Joseph Smith Lecture 6: Joseph Smith as Teacher, Speaker, and Counselor
ds: The qualities and experiences that made Joseph Smith a teacher, speaker, and counselor for those around him, focusing on his time in Kirtland.

t: Joseph Smith Lecture 5: Joseph Smith and the Kirtland Temple
ds: Truman Madsen describes the experiences and sacrifices of Joseph Smith and the Saints in Kirtland, Ohio while building the temple.

t: Joseph Smith Lecture 3: Joseph Smith and Spiritual Gifts
ds: Truman Madsen discusses spiritual gifts and how Joseph Smith used them to bless the Saints and teach them the fulness of the gospel.

t: Joseph Smith Lecture 4: Joseph Smith and Trials
ds: An account of Joseph Smith’s trials and the effects of the hardship on his family, his friends, his life, and his character.

t: Joseph Smith Lecture 2: Joseph’s Personality and Character
ds: Using quotes and stories from those who personally knew Joseph Smith, Truman Madsen describes the Prophet’s personality and character.

t: Joseph Smith Lecture 1: The First Vision and Its Aftermath
ds: Truman Madsen speaks on Joseph Smith’s early life, First Vision, and life in the aftermath, including lessons, experiences, and consequences.
Elder McConkie testifies that the revelation extending priesthood blessings to those of all nations and races is divine and that "all are alike unto God."
Missionary work is thriving, because the honest hearts of sincere missionaries are connecting with the honest hearts of sincere people.

t: The Faith, Strength, and Service of Youth
ds: The Church is growing rapidly. Repent, help youth serve missions, stretch your soul in service, and be the Savior’s hands in the last days.
The scientific method is a powerful way of finding truth, but when it is paired with spiritual insight and faith.
Sometimes we get lost on the path to eternal life. Loving the Lord enough to keep His commandments will help keep us on track to return to Him.
God desires all His children to return to Him, but the conflict of life is to choose between eternity's blessings and compromising for worldly things.
In a time when the Church experiences great growth throughout the world, we need to prepare to be its leaders, and our preparation begins with testimony.
God's plan of salvation hinges on the atoning sacrifice of Jesus Christ. In return for His love, can we not make our own small sacrifices for Him?

t: “If Thou Wilt Be Perfect, . . . Come and Follow Me”
ds: Constant study of the gospel will help you in developing the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to be guided by the Spirit in following the Savior.

t: “Serious About the Things to Be Done”
ds: As we get serious about our covenants and look for the Lord's plan in our lives, we will see the blessings waiting for us.

t: “Because I Live, Ye Shall Live Also”
ds: Because of the Resurrection of Christ, we know that there is life after death. Families are eternal, and our departed loved ones are not far.

t: The Christ of the Book of Mormon
ds: The Christ of the Book of Mormon offers Christianity a clearer picture of the Savior, His plan for us, and His doctrine.
There is a necessary refining process in adversity which increases our understanding, enhances our sensitivity, and makes us more Christlike.

t: “And the Greatest of These Is Love”
ds: Love is not just an investment; it is an adventure. It is not an idyllic dream; it happens. President Hinckley reminds us of the sacred nature of love.
The world is pulling women further away from their divine roles. We must teach our daughters about the gospel of Jesus Christ, but still allow them to fly.
Jesus Christ was and is uniquely qualified to be our Redeemer because of His pre-mortal foreordination, His mortal perfection, and His eternal atonement.
Just like the law of gravity, there are laws that the Lord has put in place to guide and direct His children back to Him.
This Christmas, Marion D. Hanks shares important lessons about overcoming adversity, and about the intense love, justice, and mercy of God.
N. Eldon Tanner explains the organization and administration of the restored Church and how departments work in tandem to accomplish the Lord's work.
Christ is not only the miraculous baby of Bethlehem or the atoning Savior of Gethsemane. He is also our creator, the source of our existence.

t: N. Eldon Tanner: An Example to Follow
ds: Marvin J. Ashton takes an opportunity to hold up the example of President N. Eldon Tanner. His humility, integrity, and kindness are worth emulating.

t: “He Hath Given a Law unto All Things”
ds: Technology enables incredible growth of the Church. God has appointed a law unto all things, and He has a hand in this continuing progress.

tp: Church Jesus Christ Latter Day Saints Mormons
ds: Satan knows Christ for who He is and the Church for what it is. When all hell is moved in opposition, stand fast in your testimony of truth.
Everything we do in this life, especially living worthy of a celestial marriage, prepares us to become like our Father in Heaven.
Paul H. Dunn explains that "no one can make you feel inferior without your consent." If you know your worth, you can succeed.
LeGrand Richards shares some reminiscences from his many years in missionary work for the Church.

t: A New Era of Growth and Development
ds: Many are called upon to be modern-day pioneers. By asking "Golden Questions," members can support full-time missionaries as the Church grows and develops.
President Kimball teaches that absolute truth exists and testifies of some truths, such as the Atonement, the Apostasy, and the Restoration.
You have divine purpose and responsibility. Follow “the Law” and “the Way,” keeping Christ's commandments and being an example of Him.

t: Temples Now and in the Future
ds: Spencer W. Kimball, speaking of temples now and in the future, tells of a time when temples will be operating night and day to accomplish the Lord's work.

t: The Joyous Obligation of Missionary Work
ds: Through missionary work, we can participate with God in the saving of souls—a joyous obligation for those who love the Lord.
Richard H. Cracroft shares some of the twists, turns, and tools on our trek through the wilderness of life as we journey to a spiritual Canaan.
Victor L. Brown emphasizes the importance for men to exercise the priesthood righteously and for women to magnify their unique influence.
"What is man?" Thanks to the knowledge we have of the Plan of Salvation, we can know of our divine heritage and destiny as children of God.
God will save our generation by sending Elijah with priesthood sealing keys to connect us with our forefathers and our posterity.
The world offers transitory pleasures, but only obedience brings happiness. Are you obedient to the scriptural commandments of God and to prophetic counsel?

Learning to listen to the promptings of the Spirit brings safety. Every worthy individual is entitled to the companionship of the Spirit. If you listen, you will find he is often more eager to help than we are to obey.

t: What It Means to Establish a Relationship with Christ
ds: We all have a divine potential to become like Christ, but to become like Him, we must develop a relationship with Him by praying, repenting, and obeying.
Food storage prepares us for famine, but are we prepared for emotional, mental, and spiritual famine? Books help us prepare for those times.

t: A Vision and a Hope for the Youth of Zion
ds: Learn to live the law of consecration, a celestial law—not to be confused with communism and socialism, which take away agency.

t: God’s Hand in Our Nation’s History
ds: The study of history is insightful and important. Don't be afraid to add to the secular and humanistic a spiritual view of American history.
Home storage is more than food storage or financial preparedness. Your spirituality and family relationships are all the home storage you can take with you.
At the dedication of the enlarged Harold B. Lee library, President Marion G. Romney shares insights about the importance of knowledge and truth.

t: Soul-Butter and Hogwash: Mark Twain and Frontier Religion
ds: Mark Twain's early experience with religion gives us insight into American history and culture and this author's life and literature.
People are happier when they lose themselves in the service of others. Forget yourself and reach out. You will be happier when you do.
We can experience happiness now and enjoy it by doing three simple things: serve others, express love to those around us, and never give up.
God gave us the freedom to choose but not the freedom to choose our consequences. To become our best selves, we must choose the right.
When we have important decisions to make, the counsel of prophets and the power of prayer, together with the will to act, will guide us to our potential.
Parents are responsible to raise their children righteously. It is a blessing to care for God's spirit children.
Sometimes when Church leaders give counsel, there are exceptions. Follow the rule first, and trust that God will let you know if you are an exception.
In an incredible testament to Joseph Smith’s divine calling, James A. Cullimore retells several events from the life of Joseph Smith, the Mormon prophet.
Elder Perry and members of his family witness how we need the Lord for our physical, social, emotional, mental, and spiritual well-being.
Don't be like the man who, in the parable of the king's wedding feast, appeared without the proper clothes. Get spiritually dressed; prepare to meet God.
N. Eldon Tanner shares some fundamental principles for living a successful life—and, even more importantly, preparing for eternal life.
The gospel is God’s plan for our eternal success. Here are some fundamentals for achieving both temporal and spiritual success.

t: Celestial Marriage—A Little Heaven on Earth

t: Art and Culture in Everyday Life

ds: Elder Joseph Fielding Smith speaks of historical and current events, especially in the Middle East, as fulfillment of prophecy given in the scriptures.
In this devotional, Stephen L. Richards speaks of the duty of both men and women to honor and live worthily of the priesthood.
Through stories from history, we see that following the oracle of God, the prophet, is how we can receive guidance and protection from God.
The growth of the Church is accelerating to fulfill prophecy and to bless God's children. This is a special time to be on the earth.
Preston Nibley offers historical and personal insights into each of the latter-day presidents of the Church from Joseph Smith to David O. McKay.
Why is it important to marry in the faith, and in the temple? Because blessings await our families that can be found only through eternal covenants.

t: What Men and Women Are Tomorrow Depends upon What You Do Today
ds: You are the men and women of tomorrow, and your actions today matter not only for the future of this world, but for your future in eternity.
President Clark shares his testimony of the magnificence, love, and mission of each member of the Godhead: our Father, our Savior, and the Holy Spirit.
You cannot buy integrity with any sum of money; you can only cultivate a good name for yourself throughout your life by the way you conduct yourself.
Thomas L. Martin humorously describes the main events of his life and highlights how the hand of the Lord worked to help him reach all his righteous goals.
Bryant S. Hinckley commemorates the efforts of others in establishing BYU and reminds students to remember the heritage and potential of this institution.

Joseph Fielding Smith recounts the testimonies of the witnesses to the Book of Mormon and the restoration of the priesthood. The importance of their testimonies is in keeping with the Lord's law of divine witnesses.
Elder Harold B. Lee shares some life advice for graduates, whether they are heading into business, military, or homemaking: don't forget the Lord your God.
To Brigham Young University graduates, President David O. McKay speaks on how we can live a variety of eternal truths to improve our lives.
Lack of knowledge of church history does not mean that we must doubt. We must only keep searching for the truth, whether by history or faith.

t: The World Today and Latter-day Saint College Students
ds: Milton R. Hunter speaks about concerns of Latter-day Saint college students in a world whose political and moral dynamics are so uncertain.
As the world becomes increasingly dismissive of the morality, we must create a style of our own—one of modesty and chastity.
In this brief fireside testimony, John A. Widtsoe reminds us that a testimony is living. Having one today does not mean that it will be here tomorrow.
As the central government's power ever increases, we must protect our political freedom and show that we will take a stand as members of the Church.
With reference to BYU football and the United States military, Elder Harold B. Lee speaks about loyalty. Where is our loyalty? Are we prepared to meet God?

t: Leadership: the Salt of the Earth
ds: If we are to become, as Christ commanded, the "salt of the earth," we must be prepared for academic, business, and civic leadership in the world.
History gives us many examples of leaders, but true leadership is being righteous and leading others to eternal life.

t: True Christianity: The Ideal for Humanity
Accounting for the Lord Jesus Christ
ds: History talks of prominent historical figures, but often skips over the Savior. Accounting for the Lord means learning from His teachings.

tp: Church Jesus Christ Latter Day Saints Mormons
ds: Ezra Taft Benson teaches about the Church's unique message for the world, and how that message brings opposition, but also success and happiness.

t: Four Cornerstones upon Which to Build Greatness
ds: Greatness comes through faith, education, industry, and cooperation—each understood through a gospel lens, as John A. Widtsoe teaches.
A BYU president shares five habits that will carry us through the journey of life: learning, loving, thinking, appreciation, and worship.
The law of divine witnesses adds credibility to Joseph Smith's testimony of the Book of Mormon and the restoration of the priesthood.
Elder Clark examines some of the common diseases that plague men's characters and shows that Christ gives spiritual healing.
A strong testimony of the gospel of Jesus Christ takes effort—but is well worth it. Testimony can carry you through the challenges of life.

t: Raising the World to a Higher Plane of Morality
ds: The morality of the world can be no greater than the goodness of its individuals. Use knowledge and God's guidance to make the world better.

t: The Charted Course of the Church in Education

ds: Brigham Young University is the Church university, and it has an emphasis on God and the gospel over than any other truths.
Karl G. Maeser offers a final address as principal of the Brigham Young Academy, praising and blessing it for future generations.
